label: <DEL> step of short sequences (L<=5) starting with u/f/d/k/p/b/h
explanation: Mostly a delimiter-step unit: 82% of activation mass is on the <DEL> step (recall_idx 0) and it never fires in the copy phase. At <DEL> it fires mainly in short sequences (rate 11% at L=3, 4% at L=4, falling to 0.2% for L>=7). Whether it fires depends on sequence content: first/output tokens u, d, f, b, h, k, p have 3-5x lift, and many digits suppress it. The top activations are all <DEL> in L=3-4 sequences like "k p n <DEL>" and "f k s <DEL>". The other ~18% of mass is weak firing during the original phase at t=2-4 on the first occurrence of t, x or c (also q, 3), but this part is noisy. Dev scores: <DEL> & L<=5 & first token in {u,f,d,k,p,b,h} gives P 0.68 / R 0.41 / F1 0.51 / mass recall 0.59; <DEL> & L<=5 alone gives mass recall 0.78 at P 0.25. The content dependence is graded rather than a clean token set, so precision and recall are both incomplete.
